subject.title: fix(whatsapp): harden bridge and server lifecycle

question: Should Crabline permanently remove non-loopback WhatsApp server binds, or preserve an explicit external deployment mode for TLS-terminated and isolated environments?
rationale: The branch intentionally trades an existing independently usable server mode for a stricter credential-exposure boundary, and code review cannot choose that compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Secure default with opt-in
options.body: Default to loopback but permit a clearly named external mode with strong warnings, TLS or proxy requirements, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Accept the breaking restriction
options.body: Keep the unconditional rejection and explicitly approve the startup break with concrete migration guidance for affected deployments.

options.title: Add native TLS first
options.body: Pause the restriction until the server supports remote provider endpoints through built-in TLS configuration.

recommendation.title: Secure default with opt-in
recommendation.body: Default to loopback but permit a clearly named external mode with strong warnings, TLS or proxy requirements, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available history-linked routing candidate for the original WhatsApp channel and server surface.
